questions.q: Why can't Castlebridge move a flow built outside of any solution into another environment?
options: Flows outside a solution have no supported way to move between environments
Flows can only ever run in the environment with the most storage
Only flows with a trigger can be moved
Moving flows always requires a Microsoft support ticket
questions.explain: A flow on its own lives only in the environment it was created in. A solution packages the flow with its related components so it can be deployed elsewhere.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the Test environment in the Dev / Test / Prod pattern?
options: It's where dispatchers run the flow against real shipments
It's an optional backup copy of Production
It's where the solution is validated against realistic data before anyone outside the automation team touches it
It's where makers permanently store finished, retired flows
questions.explain: Test (or QA) exists to validate a solution with realistic data after Development but before Production, catching problems where they're still cheap to fix.

questions.q: What does a pipeline in the Power Platform Admin Center actually automate?
options: Writing the flow's trigger and action logic for the maker
Exporting, validating, and importing a solution into the next environment stage
Generating a new DLP policy automatically
Converting a cloud flow into a desktop flow
questions.explain: A pipeline automates the export/validate/import sequence that would otherwise be done by hand at every stage, triggered by a maker clicking Deploy.

questions.q: What's the key difference between an unmanaged and a managed solution?
options: Managed solutions run faster than unmanaged ones
Unmanaged solutions can only exist in Production
A managed solution is locked against direct editing, while an unmanaged solution is still fully editable
There is no functional difference, only a naming convention
questions.explain: Unmanaged solutions are editable, which is appropriate during active development. Managed solutions are locked, which prevents uncontrolled edits once a solution reaches Test or Production.

questions.q: Why does locking Test and Production solutions as managed matter for Castlebridge specifically?
options: It prevents someone in Production from quietly editing the live flow and drifting it out of sync with Development
It makes the flow's run history permanently visible to everyone
It automatically fixes any DLP policy violations
It removes the need for a Development environment entirely
questions.explain: Locking managed solutions in Test and Production stops a well-meaning but uncontrolled edit from happening outside the Dev-to-Prod pipeline, keeping every environment's version of the flow consistent.
